description: A water point database of community wells in Harare, Zimbabwe, curated by MSF for its cholera and typhoid response and used for mapping and modelling. Contents: the OpenStreetMap wiki import page says MSF collected locations, infrastructure and operational arrangements for 458 water points, with a unique ID, the infrastructure in place (for example hand pump or electric submersible pump), the working status of the borehole and whether the water is for drinking. Producer: MSF, whose data was shared for OpenStreetMap in March 2019 after explicit permission on 4 February 2019. Coverage: Harare. Format and access: a CSV with latitude, longitude and attributes shared through a Google Drive folder linked from the wiki; not checked from the cloud. Licence: stated on the wiki page as public domain, by permission granted by email. Caveats: a single-organisation snapshot from 2019; the page says it was the most up-to-date data for Harare at the time and proposes that its coordinates override OpenStreetMap positions; updates depend on MSF and the Zimbabwean OpenStreetMap community. Simulation uses: water access and outage impact in urban drinking water and outbreak response models. Related records: none identified.
